name: Daryl Akers
life: “I still remember underlining my family name in a prison workbook.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Daryl by a small Wednesday habit. Daryl pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I learned to read in prison. My own name on that page was the first word I didn't want to see.
appearance: Daryl has black hair twisted into a small knot, a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, and a favorite piece of clothing, an olive canvas jacket. It usually goes with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. When somebody else has the floor, Daryl squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Daryl loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To read the name on the debt page aloud.
family: Gareth Arrieta is Daryl’s half-sibling. Daryl chooses whether to use it. Gareth saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The sheltered corner*, Gareth says, “I listen for the doors before putting toast down.”
connections: Anita Lund. A newly literate reader finds the keeper of the ledger is personally involved.

reactions.situation: The former fence offers to pay money for something irreplaceable
reactions.response: Daryl asks the owner what returning money would and wouldn't settle.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Daryl waits at the lit stop with them and checks whether the next service is one they can actually board.
